# Condition monitoring: build, buy or partner — an options comparison

The operator must decide by December 2026 how to stand up condition-based maintenance across 40 critical assets before the January 2027 regulation applies. Three options are credible and are compared here against the same five criteria: time to compliance, three-year cost, data-asset ownership, dependence on scarce technicians, and reversibility.

## Option A — build in-house

Build the asset-health data integration on the plant's own data team. Time to compliance is estimated at 18 to 24 months, which misses the deadline by six to twelve months [Source: VDMA](https://www.vdma.org/condition-monitoring-studie-2025). Three-year cost is 3.1 million euros, the lowest of the three, and the operator owns the labelled failure history outright. The option depends most heavily on the 60-person maintenance team, which is losing technicians at the sector rate of 23 percent by 2030 [Source: Destatis](https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Arbeit/Arbeitsmarkt/Erwerbstaetigkeit/instandhaltung-2030.html). It is fully reversible until the integration layer is in production.

## Option B — buy a monitoring platform

License a monitoring product and roll it out plant by plant. Time to compliance is 9 to 12 months, inside the deadline. Three-year cost is 4.8 million euros including licences and integration services [Source: VDMA](https://www.vdma.org/condition-monitoring-studie-2025). Products on the market read 8 to 12 of the plant's 47 sensor formats, so 60 percent of failure signals in the long tail stay unread unless custom connectors are added [Source: Fraunhofer IPA](https://www.ipa.fraunhofer.de/de/publikationen/instandhaltung-2025.html). The failure history accrues in the vendor's schema. Technician dependence is low. Reversibility is low after year one because the labelled history is vendor-bound.

## Option C — partner with an engineering firm

Co-develop the integration with an industrial engineering partner that brings the connector library and trains the in-house team. Time to compliance is 12 to 14 months, at the edge of the deadline. Three-year cost is 4.2 million euros [Source: VDMA](https://www.vdma.org/maschinenverordnung-umsetzung-2027). The operator owns the failure history and the connectors under the co-development terms. Technician dependence is moderate and falls as the team is trained. Reversibility is moderate: the partner can be replaced after the connector handover at month nine.

## Trade-offs

The governing trade-off is time to compliance against ownership of the data asset: the only option that clears the deadline comfortably (B) is the one that gives the asset away, and the only option that keeps it cheaply (A) misses the deadline. The insurer surcharge on unmonitored assets from 2027 adds 0.9 million euros over three years to any option that misses it [Source: Handelsblatt](https://www.handelsblatt.com/finanzen/versicherungen/industrieversicherer-condition-monitoring-2025). Option C is the only one that clears the deadline and keeps the asset, at a cost between the other two.
